\chapter{Synthesis --- Real Conditions}
\label{ch:sintesis-condicion}
\hlchaptermodality{198}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say what happens, or will happen, if something else does.}

I can say what happens, or will happen, if something else does.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[Practice]{Synthesis — real conditions}

\label{lesson:ES-C55-sintesis-condicion}



\begin{quote}
Which tense after \emph{si}? (\textbf{Present}, always.) Which after the comma? (\textbf{Present or future} — your choice of meaning.)
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Two chapters, one word, and a sentence shape you did not have before:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{} & \textbf{} \\
\midrule
\emph{Si tengo tiempo, hablo español.} & a habit — whenever it happens \\
\emph{Si tengo tiempo, hablaré español.} & a plan — this once \\
\emph{Si llueve, comeré en casa.} & a decision waiting on the weather \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

\textbf{This is the first thing in the book that needs two clauses to say.} Every sentence before it was one thought. A condition is two, hooked together — and the hook cost you no new grammar at all, only a word and a rule about where the future may stand.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: what a condition is for}]
A condition lets you talk about a world you are not claiming is real yet. That is a genuinely new power, and it is the doorway to the rest of this book: once you can suppose, you can also suppose things that are \textbf{not} true — \emph{if I had time} — and that needs a verb form you do not have yet.

You will meet it soon. For now the supposing is real, and real supposing is most of what anyone says all day.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a real condition about your own day
  \item the same one, moved into the future
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
How many clauses does a condition need? (\textbf{Two}.) What new verb form did it cost you? (\textbf{None}.) And what is still missing? (A way to suppose something \textbf{untrue} — that comes next.)
\end{tcolorbox}
